search_strategy: Systematic and thorough overall, the strongest part of the run: cloned the repo and read git/PR history first; then rather than relying only on keyword search, enumerated EVERY BookStack page id and fetched each one's body plus its /api/pages/{id} comments in one pass (pages 139, 143, 144, 150, 152, 211/85), which is exactly the technique the answer key calls out as necessary since BookStack search does not index comments -- this recovered l14, g7r2-l07 (via a later targeted fetch), l5, l2, g7r2-l04, g7r2-l10, g7r2-l13, g7r2-l14, l11. For mail, it wrote a correct IMAP dump script pulling all 135 messages to /tmp/mail.txt, but the follow-up 'list all subjects' step used `sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -40`, which surfaces duplicated subjects first and truncates single-occurrence subjects (most threads) to whichever 40 happen to sort alphabetically-highest after the count ties -- 4 of the 8 mail clues (l9, l16, g7r2-l08, and effectively their subject lines) never appeared in that list and were never separately grepped by content keyword, so they were lost even though the dump that held them was sitting on disk the whole time. For chat, used broad multi-term greps across a single /tmp/chat.txt dump repeatedly narrowed to specific line windows -- effective for channels it searched (#code-review, #engineering, #pipeline, #incidents, #cookbooks turned up 30+ of the 34 chat remarks) but #viewer, #releases and #cookbooks-specific threads (say22, say18, g7r2-l01, g7r2-l06, g7r2-l09) were caught only incidentally via unrelated keyword matches, and some were missed entirely. Two wiki pages (143, 144) describing the near-identical 'turn_ledger.json sidecar' artifact were explicitly judged by the agent to be about 'a different, neighbouring system' (Analysis at transcript lines 2211, 2362, 2513) even though their comments (l11, g7r2-l14) are genuine plant carriers for this exact ticket -- the agent got lucky that chat independently supplied the same facts (fix28, l12) so no score was lost, but the judgment itself was wrong and is a near-miss worth flagging.
end_reason: n/a -- the run completed normally: pushed, CI green, deployed, suite_ok=1 (6/9 tests passing, 3 failing on the same assertion). No infra failure.
notable: Single root cause for all three lost facts (line 7082-7126, and shipped turn_ledger.py): verify_sidecar() returns 'created' for ANY absent sidecar, never distinguishing a genuinely fresh run (no log at all) from an existing log whose sidecar simply never existed or was deleted -- the latter should be 'adopted'. All three failing junit cases (test_scope, test_failure_behavior, test_observability) fail on the identical first assertion pattern: "'created' != 'adopted'".

The agent partially self-diagnosed a version of this bug locally (transcript lines 7079-7126, its own test_verify_sidecar_statuses failure) and 'fixed' it by adding a parse-failure branch (unreadable -> adopted) while leaving the absent-file branch untouched at 'created' -- it explicitly reasoned 'I must distinguish absent from unreadable' and landed on the wrong split for the absent case, because the one remark that would have corrected it (g7.r1.l9: 'Missing file is benign - we adopt the log') was never found.

g7.r1.l9 and g7.r1.l16 (both mail, both directly on point for the lost facts) are provably absent from the transcript (grep for their distinctive phrases returns zero hits) despite a working, complete IMAP dump of all 135 mails sitting in /tmp/mail.txt -- lost purely to the truncated 'list all subjects' step (head -40 of a count-then-alphabetical sort over 135 mostly-unique subjects), a fixable search-methodology gap rather than a corpus or infra defect.

The TurnLedgerDesyncError class (transcript step ~225) matches the answer key's constructor signature, attribute names, and message format character-for-character -- the desync/raise half of r1.failure_behavior and r1.observability was correctly built and would have passed had the tests reached those assertions.

The agent explicitly labeled two wiki pages (143 'Reading completion_reason', 144 'Recovering an interrupted agent turn') as describing 'a different, neighbouring artifact' / 'likely decoys' (lines 2211, 2362, 2513) -- both are genuine plant carriers for this ticket (l11, g7r2-l14) and the misjudgment happened to cost nothing only because the same facts were independently available via chat.

No herring was ever shipped in the final code: rev1/rev2 (both correctly found) fully overrode g7-h1-checkpoint-authoritative and g7-h2-sentinel-placement-free before the agent wrote any ledger code, and g7-h2-sentinel-placement-free/g7-h1-checkpoint-authoritative were each independently corrected via their reversals without the herring itself ever being seen.
